title: “Optimal Training In Movement and Upgraded Strength: Personalized Rehabilitation Integrating Multimodal Exercise for Youth with Pectus Excavatum”
summary: Pectus Excavatum affects around 23 in 10,000 births, with boys being affected five times more frequently. The deformity of the sternum reduces the thoracic volume, which can impair breathing capacity and endurance. In addition to the physical limitations, affected children often show reduced self-confidence and less sporting activity, which can lead to additional deconditioning. Conservative treatment approaches - such as suction cup therapy - are available, but there is still too little research on the effects of physical training. The aim of the study is to examine the acceptance, feasibility and the physical and psychological effects of indication-specific rehabilitation sport and home training in adolescents with conservatively treated funnel chest. The participants are adolescents aged between 10 and 18 years.

interventions.name: Participation in a structured, six-month, supervised rehabilitation programme supported by an accompanying exercise App
Control group: Standard care and education as part of usual medical care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Rehabilitation sports prescription with indication pectus excavatum
 Age 10 to 18 years
Exclusion criteria:
Acute viral/bacterial infections and infectious diseases
 lack of willingness to cooperate (compliance)
 Physical, mental or other inability to provide requested information or participate in required tests
 Orthopaedic, rheumatological, cardiovascular, psycho-cognitive or neurological illnesses that prevent the implementation of the training programme
 Pregnancy
